One man, One Mission

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After explosive allegations by KZN Police Commissioner Lt Gen Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi that the Police Minister and other top brass are colluding with 'drug cartels', we dig past the spin to reveal the rot

Unique Selling Point:
In an extraordinary press conference, KZN top cop Provincial Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi turned whistelblower – taking aim at the country’s criminal elite.

During the briefing, which Mkhwanazi addressed to the citizens of South Africa, he announced that the disbandment of the KZN Political Killings Task Team by high level officials was directly linked to their involvement in an investigation into a drug cartel that has corrupted high level politicians - including the Minister of Police.

Since its establishment in July 2018, the Political Killings Task Team investigated 612 dockets, secured over 100 convictions, and helped crack syndicate-linked murders in Gauteng and at the University of Fort Hare.

Mkhwanazi said pressure to disband the unit grew after its ballistic experts linked weapons found in Gauteng to several high-profile killings, including cases involving South African musicians.


Summary:
Since then President Ramaphosa has promised a judicial commission of enquiry and put Minister Senzo Mchunu on a leave of absence. Many have expressed their disappointment at the seeming lack of a sense of urgency around the allegations, especially around the 6 month time line for the enquiry and the fact that the minister is still in his position. But these allegations, if proven to be true, speak to the very heart of the capture of the justice cluster by organised crime syndicates.
We will connect the dots for viewers, explore the different allegations and provide some much needed clarity on how all the role-players fit together. We are witnessing one of the biggest shake ups in the history of the SAPS - and the man making the allegations is by far the most senior police official to ever do so.

Further information:
-We have some of the WhatsApp messages mentioned by Gen Mkhwanazi
-Investigative journalist Jeff Wicks will provide important background on one of the alleged criminals named in the presser, tender king Vusimusi 'The Cat' Matlala and how he is linked to three shelf companies that were part of a syndicate that fleeced the Tembisa Hospital of R2.3 billion (the same investigation that led to the murder of whistleblower Babita Deokaran). And how, while he was under investigation for that crime, he managed to be awarded a SAPS tender for healthcare worth R360 million.
-We can also link Matlala to another figure Carte Blanche has investigated - Shauwn Mkhize.
-Matlala is currently standing trial for attempted murder, along with his wife, Tsakani, who once posted on social media how a blue light brigade was taking her children to school. He remains in custody in C-Max in PTA. His next court date is 26 August, when more charges from two other cases are expected to be merged with the current case.
- We will question the link between Matlala and a man named Oupa Brown Mogotsi - who received a payment from Matlala's company, Medicare 24 Tshwane District - the same company that won the now cancelled SAPS contract - allegedly for his help in getting the Political Killings Task Team disbanded.
-Mogotsi is an enigmatic figure, who claims to have experience working in the 'underground' of intelligence circles.
- Minister Mchunu is on the record claiming not to know Brown Mogotsi in parliament, but he has since admitted that he is a 'comrade'. Mchunu, Mogotsi and Matlala are linked through financial transactions linked to political events and a gala dinner.
- We will ask why Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya has allegedly been sitting on case dockets that were removed from the political killings task team for months, some of them with warrants of arrest already applied for.
-We will attempt to get an interview with Brown Mogotsi - he has spoken to other media.
- Matala is behind bars

Extra Budget Items:
We may need to buy images/footage of Mogotsi and Matlala.
We may need to travel to KZN
